correctness.rationale: For r_j=H_{j+1}/H_j, positivity forces R>max r_j and fixes each P_j=log(R/r_j) for j=0,1,2. Equating cH_0 reconstructed at the first two parasitoid updates gives exactly the displayed F=0. Either admissible root gives a positive c and P_0 and regenerates the observations, so the elimination loses no conditions. Writing L=log 2 and b=sqrt 2, the two trajectories give P_1=L/2 and 3L/2 and then P_2=L(1-1/b) and 2L(1-1/(2b)), respectively. These imply H_1=1, H_2=b and H_3=b exp(L/b) for both. At r_0=1 and r_1=b, differentiating each quotient at equality with common value K gives the derivative difference (1-K)(1/(R-1)-1/(R-b)). Since K=L at 2 and 2L at 4, the roots are simple with opposite signs. The implicit-function theorem gives locally unique branches in disjoint admissible neighborhoods; reconstruction and the invertible H_0-plus-ratios chart give openness in four real host coordinates. Nonconstancy persists because r_1 is bounded away from 1. The common r_2 cancels from the difference in P_3, leaving Lb and fifth-census log ratio L(1-b). This proves neither an exact count of all roots nor general five-census recovery.
